metadata.summary: Noah Okafor scored twice as Leeds beat Chelsea 4-1 to record their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years.
metadata.content: Chelsea 1-4 Leeds (Nov 21, 2026) Game Analysis - ESPN Skip to main content Skip to navigation Premier League Chelsea Chelsea CHE 5-1-5 , 16 PTS 1 5-1-5 , 16 PTS FT Leeds United Leeds LEE 4-5-2 , 17 PTS 4 4-5-2 , 17 PTS Emmanuel Emegha - 25' Noah Okafor - 28', 58' Dominic Calvert-Lewin - 53' Pen Brenden Aaronson - 90'+1' Chelsea v Leeds By PA Updated: Nov 21, 2026, 12:22 pm Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email Chelsea stunned Leeds for their first win at Stamford Bridge in almost 30 years. Silvina Brodersohn - CameraSport via Getty Images Noah Okafor scored twice as Leeds beat Chelsea 4-1 to record their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Daniel Farke's team conceded six here earlier this season. That wild defeat in the Carabao Cup in September came at a time when Chelsea were playing cavalier football that made a 6-3 scoreline seem normal, but they stand now on the brink watching their season fall apart. This was not what their supporters were sold when Xabi Alonso was appointed amidst broad smiles six months ago. The leadership spoke then of lessons having been learned and of a corner turned. What must co-owner Behdad Eghbali and his four-strong team of sporting directors have made of Leeds running rings around their team on their own pitch, cantering to an easy victory with minimal resistance? They began well here, 23-year-old striker Emmanuel Emegha firing them ahead early on his full debut, but within minutes they had gifted Okafor an equaliser,

messages.text: Late Thomason strike powers Wrexham to much-needed away win

metadata.summary: George Thomason grabbed a late winner as Wrexham secured a welcome 1-0 victory away at Lincoln.
metadata.content: Lincoln City 0-1 Wrexham (Nov 21, 2026) Game Analysis - ESPN Skip to main content Skip to navigation EFL Championship Lincoln City Lincoln City LCN 4-3-9 , 15 PTS 0 4-3-9 , 15 PTS FT Wrexham Wrexham WXM 5-6-5 , 21 PTS 1 5-6-5 , 21 PTS George Thomason - 82' Lincoln City v Wrexham By PA Nov 21, 2026, 12:49 pm Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email George Thomason grabbed a late winner as Wrexham secured a welcome 1-0 victory away at Lincoln. It was a game lacking real quality in the final third at Sincil Bank, but Thomason kept his cool when the moment arose to fire Wrexham to victory with his 82nd-minute strike. It was a first away league victory for Phil Parkinson's side since the start of September when they beat Millwall 2-0. The Red Dragons have now gone three games without defeat and will be hoping to use their recent upturn in form as a catalyst towards their playoff push. For Lincoln, it was the latest bump in the road as the reality of being minnows in the Championship is really beginning to hit home. Wrexham earned a much-needed away victory at Lincoln. Andrew Vaughan/Getty Images Any hopes the international break would bring about a change in fortunes were dashed with a fourth loss on the spin, whilst it is their seventh defeat in nine. Their only victory in that time was the 4-1 hammering of relegation rivals Burnley, which led to Nicky Hayen's sacking. messages.text: Alcaraz defeats Shelton to reach championship match at ATP Finals

metadata.summary: Carlos Alcaraz made it a lucky 13 wins in a row against Ben Shelton to reach Sunday's showpiece of the ATP Finals in Turin.
metadata.content: Carlos Alcaraz: Seven-time Grand Slam champion sinks Ben Shelton to reach championship match at ATP Finals | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Carlos Alcaraz: Seven-time Grand Slam champion sinks Ben Shelton to reach championship match at ATP Finals Carlos Alcaraz advances to the championship match at the Nitto ATP Finals for the second consecutive year; you can watch the climax to the ATP Finals in Turin this weekend on Sky Sports Tennis Saturday 21 November 2026 16:05, UK Image: Carlos Alcaraz is through to Sunday's showpiece at the ATP Finals in Turin Carlos Alcaraz made it a lucky 13 wins in a row against Ben Shelton to reach Sunday's showpiece of the ATP Finals in Turin. Alcaraz, who eased concerns about a hamstring ‌injury by completing an unbeaten group-stage campaign, defeated American third seed Shelton 3-6 6-3 7-6 (7-1) despite heavy strapping on his upper left leg. The Spaniard was beaten by Jannik Sinner in last year's final in Turin but will be determined to go one better this time around and claim his first year-end title. He will face either Alexander Zverev or Daniil Medvedev in Sunday's championship match. metadata.content: Haydock: Dan Skelton's Grey Dawning oozes class in Betfair Chase repeat | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Haydock: Dan Skelton's Grey Dawning oozes class in Betfair Chase repeat The Dan Skelton-trained Grey Dawning showed his quality when defending his Betfair Chase crown at the expense of Jagwar in Haydock's National Hunt feature; the winner is now a 10-1 chance for the Ryanair Chase at the Cheltenham Festival Saturday 21 November 2026 16:38, UK Image: Grey Dawning won the Betfair Chase for a second successive year Grey Dawning joined an illustrious list when following up his success of 12 months ago with a smooth performance in the Betfair Chase at Haydock. Having seen off Royale Pagaille last year, this time Dan Skelton's grey found Jagwar a tougher adversary. Jagwar jumped with aplomb throughout for Harry Cobden, but made his first mistake at the third last which handed the initiative to Grey Dawning and Harry Skelton. However, Jagwar came back for more and it was not until Grey Dawning showed his superior speed after the final fence the contest was over, as the 11-10 favourite went on to win by three and three-quarter lengths.
